title: The Missing Alternative
fact_notes: オリジナル教材。架空の人物・出来事による例であり、実在の調査や実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A student deciding whether to take part in a weekend activity writes a list of reasons for accepting the invitation and another list of reasons for refusing it.
sentences.ja: 週末活動への参加を決める生徒は招待を受ける理由と断る理由の二つの一覧を書く。

sentences.en: She carefully examines both lists, but she finds it difficult to choose between the available options.
sentences.ja: 両一覧を慎重に検討するが利用可能な選択肢から選ぶことは難しい。

sentences.en: A friend asks why she has assumed that participation must involve remaining at the event from its beginning until its end.
sentences.ja: 友達はなぜ参加には開始から終了まで滞在する必要があると想定したか尋ねる。

sentences.en: The student suddenly recognizes that she has been evaluating a decision whose boundaries she had never examined.
sentences.ja: 生徒は境界を一度も吟味していない判断を評価していたと突然気づく。

sentences.en: Her initial description of the problem included only two possible responses.
sentences.ja: 当初の問題記述には二つの可能な反応しか含まれなかった。

sentences.en: Accepting the invitation appeared to mean sacrificing time needed for another responsibility, whereas refusing seemed to involve disappointing the people who had invited her.
sentences.ja: 招待を受けることは別の責任に必要な時間を犠牲にするように見え、断ることは招待者を失望させるように思えた。

sentences.en: The friend suggests that the organizers may be willing to discuss a different arrangement, although she cannot guarantee their response.
sentences.ja: 友人は主催者が異なる仕組みを話し合う意向があるかもしれないと提案するが返答は保証できない。

sentences.en: The student decides to inquire about the possibility of helping during part of the event before making her final decision.
sentences.ja: 最終判断前に活動の一部で手伝える可能性を問い合わせることを決める。

sentences.en: In this imagined situation, considering an additional alternative does not automatically resolve every conflict between the student's responsibilities.
sentences.ja: 仮想状況では追加選択肢の検討が生徒の責任間の全対立を自動解決するわけではない。

sentences.en: The organizers might require volunteers to be present throughout the activity for practical reasons.
sentences.ja: 主催者は実務上の理由でボランティアに活動全体への出席を求めるかもしれない。

sentences.en: Alternatively, a shorter period of assistance might involve a task different from the one that the student originally intended to perform.
sentences.ja: 別案として短時間援助は当初行うつもりだったものと異なる作業を伴い得る。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, obtaining this information would allow her to evaluate the available choices more accurately.
sentences.ja: それでも情報を得ることで選択肢をより正確に評価できるだろう。

sentences.en: The example illustrates a distinction between assessing the relative merits of several alternatives and investigating whether the alternatives initially presented describe the full range of practical possibilities.
sentences.ja: この例は複数選択肢の相対的利点の評価と、当初提示された選択肢が実務的可能性の全範囲を示すかの調査との区別を示す。

sentences.en: A person can reason carefully about an incomplete set of options and still overlook a significant opportunity.
sentences.ja: 不完全な選択肢群について慎重に推論しても重要な機会を見落とし得る。

sentences.en: Conversely, searching indefinitely for additional possibilities can delay decisions that must eventually be made.
sentences.ja: 逆に無期限に追加可能性を探すと最終的に必要な判断を遅らせ得る。

sentences.en: The challenge is to recognize assumptions that unnecessarily restrict a decision without treating every limitation as something that can be removed.
sentences.ja: 課題は全制限が除去可能と扱わず判断を不必要に制限する前提に気づくことだ。

sentences.en: Good reasoning involves more than comparing the answers that happen to be available when a question is first asked.
sentences.ja: 良い推論には問いが最初に出たときたまたま利用可能な答えを比較する以上のことが伴う。

sentences.en: It may also involve examining the way the question itself has been formulated.
sentences.ja: 問い自体がどう作られたかを調べることも伴い得る。

sentences.en: A careful decision requires attention to both the quality of the arguments and the actual range of possibilities those arguments address.
sentences.ja: 慎重な判断には論拠の質と論拠が扱う実際の可能性範囲への注意が必要だ。

sentences.en: Sometimes the most productive step is to ask whether an apparent choice between two answers is the only question worth considering.
sentences.ja: 時に最も生産的な一歩は二答間の見かけの選択が考える価値のある唯一の問いか尋ねることだ。

vocabulary.definition: giving something up for a purpose
something one is expected to do
bring a problem to a solution

questions.prompt: What is the student trying to decide?
options: Whether to take part in a weekend activity.
Which friend to invite to lunch.

questions.prompt: What does the friend's question reveal?
options: The friend has made the final decision.
The student's two options may rest on an unexamined assumption.
The student has no conflicting responsibilities.

questions.prompt: What negative consequence does accepting seem to have?
options: Losing time needed for another responsibility.
Being unable to meet the organizers.
questions.explanation_ja: 別の責任に必要な時間。

questions.prompt: Why does the student decide to inquire?
options: She wants a guarantee without asking anyone.
She has already refused the invitation.
She believes organizers have no practical constraints.
She wants to know whether partial participation is possible.
Every volunteer to perform different tasks alone.
Volunteers to remain for the entire activity.
The student to invite another friend.

questions.prompt: Why is the additional information useful even if problems remain?
options: It makes the evaluation of actual options more accurate.
It guarantees that every responsibility disappears.
It proves the organizers are wrong.
questions.explanation_ja: 現実的な選択肢を知る。

questions.prompt: What is the limitation of careful reasoning about an incomplete list?
options: A decision cannot ever be made.
Any additional option must be superior.
A useful possibility may still be overlooked.

questions.prompt: What risk accompanies an indefinite search for alternatives?

options: Expressed or developed in a particular way.

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the argument?
options: Every problem must have exactly two answers.
Searching forever is the best approach.
Practical constraints can always be eliminated.
Reasoning includes examining the way choices are defined, not only comparing existing options.
questions.explanation_ja: 選択肢の定義自体を検討。

grammar.focus: why she has assumed that participation
grammar.explanation_ja: why節はasksの内容、that節はassumedの内容。

paraphrases.source: A friend asks why she has assumed that participation must involve remaining at the event from its beginning until its end.
paraphrases.rewrite: The friend asks why the student thinks participation must last all day.

paraphrases.source: Accepting the invitation appeared to mean sacrificing time needed for another responsibility, whereas refusing seemed to involve disappointing the people who had invited her.
paraphrases.rewrite: Accepting seems to cost time, while refusing seems to disappoint others.

paraphrases.source: Nevertheless, obtaining this information would allow her to evaluate the available choices more accurately.
paraphrases.rewrite: Knowing the actual possibilities would help her judge them more accurately.

paraphrases.source: Conversely, searching indefinitely for additional possibilities can delay decisions that must eventually be made.
paraphrases.rewrite: Continuing to look for alternatives without a limit may postpone necessary decisions.

discourse.role_ja: 対立が残っても情報は有益。
探索の反対側のリスク。

cloze.explanation_ja: 可能性を問い合わせる。
